core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Ghali corresponds to the Arabic form غالي (Arabic root غ ل و (gh-l-w); غالي (Ghālī)). Its core sense is precious, dear, expensive. Ghali is Arabic غالي (Ghālī) 'dear, precious, expensive', from the root غ ل و (gh-l-w) 'to be high, exceed'. The source gloss 'heavy, burdensome, generous' conflates it with unrelated words (ثقل 'heaviness', كرم 'generosity') and has been replaced. The source records it as unisex; its better-attested usage is masculine.

The source gloss 'heavy, burdensome, generous' conflates it with unrelated words (ثقل 'heaviness', كرم 'generosity') and has been replaced. faq.a: In Urdu, Ghali is rendered غالی and carries the sense قیمتی، عزیز.

faq.q: What does Ghali mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Ghali is rendered غالی and carries the sense گران‌بها، عزیز.
A romanized syllable approximation is gha-li. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Ghali, ghali. Script forms are غالي, غالی, ग़ाली.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as unisex. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
